Validation

The builder validates two different things: the questionnaire you are authoring (is it well-formed FHIR?) and the answers entered in the preview (are they complete and valid?).

Live answer validation

As you fill in the preview, each control checks its own value and shows an inline error when something is wrong. A status indicator summarises whether the whole response is currently valid (a ✓ / ✗ badge). The checks include:

  • Required — a mandatory item must be answered.
  • Format — text must match a regular expression / expected format when one is set.
  • Text length — respect the minimum and maximum character counts.
  • Numeric range — a number must fall within its minimum / maximum value.
  • Reference type — a reference answer must point at an allowed resource type.
  • Repeat count — a repeating item must have an allowed number of entries.
  • File rules — an uploaded file must satisfy the size and type limits.

An inline error and the overall ✓/✗ badge always agree — if a field is invalid, the response is marked invalid.

Custom constraints

Beyond the built-in checks you can add your own rules with a constraint — a FHIRPath expression that must evaluate to true, paired with your own error message (questionnaire-constraint). Constraints can reference other answers via %resource, so you can express cross-field rules (e.g. "end date must be after start date"). See FHIRPath in the builder.

Questionnaire validation on import

When you load a questionnaire, the builder checks its structure and reports any problems it finds — malformed items, invalid references between items, and similar issues — so you know what you're working with before you start editing.

Among the things it reports: a Show When condition with no operator or no value to compare with, a question or display item with no text (FHIR does not require text, so this is a warning and the item is exported without it), and a group with no items (exported without an item list, because FHIR does not allow an empty one).

External FHIR validators (optional)

For authoritative validation against the FHIR specification and profiles, you can configure one or more validator servers in Settings. When set up, the builder can send the questionnaire (or response) to a validator and show the returned issues. This is optional — the live checks above work entirely in the browser with no server.

Check my form (calculated results)

Scores and calculators can hide mistakes that no single answer reveals — for example a severity band that can never be reached because a threshold was mistyped. Open ⚙ Settings ▾ → ✅ Check my form… and the builder tries many answer combinations (everything at the lowest and highest answer, one question at a time, questions left unanswered, and so on) on every calculation in the form. It then lists:

  • Some results can never appear — the text results (such as "Moderate depression") that the calculation is written to give but that no combination of answers produces. Fix the thresholds or conditions of that calculation.
  • Never shown — a question whose Show When rule none of the tried answers satisfies, so nobody could answer it. Check the rule.
  • Never produces a result — no combination of answers gives the calculation a value.
  • Not checked — the calculation reads a question that cannot be tried automatically, such as a multiple-choice list.

A date question is tried with dates around today: a day, week, month, year, 25 and 50 years before and after it, and 100 years back (a date and time question gets the same days at noon). A date limit set on the question is respected. The check cannot know whether the question is a birth date or a last-period date, so these are spread both ways; a result that needs a date far from today can be missed, and the row says so. Because the dates move with today, the answers in the report change from day to day.

A number question with no minimum or maximum is tried with numbers from 1 to 100 (a fixed spread plus a few hundred repeatable random sets, so the same form always gives the same report; if only one limit is set, the range starts or ends there). If a result needs other numbers, the row says which range was tried: set the minimum and maximum on that question to check it properly. A Show When rule that reads such a number is not judged.

Each row has a ↗ button that jumps to the calculation in the builder. Open full report opens a separate page with the questionnaire that was checked (JSON, collapsed), a summary per calculation with its formula, and one table of every answer combination that was tried: a row per combination, the answers given, and a column with the result of each calculated field. Use Print summary to keep a short printed report (per calculation: verdict, formula, the results that appeared and the ones that never did); the long table of answer combinations and the questionnaire JSON stay on screen so a large form still prints. Download answer sets (CSV) gives every answer of every combination, with a column per calculation, for a spreadsheet. The check runs entirely in your browser and changes nothing in the questionnaire.

Example: the PHQ-9 depression questionnaire

Load the PHQ-9 template (Add ▾ → templates). It has two calculated fields: PHQ-9 total score (the sum of the nine answers) and Depression severity (a text chosen from the total). Check my form reports "All 2 calculations behave as expected". The full report's table of answer combinations includes rows such as these (the answers column is shortened here):

Answers PHQ-9 total score Depression severity
no answers — —
every question "Not at all" 0 Minimal depression
every question "Nearly every day" 27 Severe depression
the first question "Nearly every day", the rest "Not at all" 3 Minimal depression
the first two questions "Nearly every day", the rest "Not at all" 6 Mild depression
the first question left unanswered, the rest "Not at all" — —

A dash means the calculation gave no result: the total is only worked out when all nine questions are answered. The whole table, a few dozen combinations in all, reaches every band up to "Moderately severe depression".

Now suppose the threshold for "Moderate depression" is mistyped, so the formula reads < 10 where it should read < 15. The report then shows, for Depression severity, "Some results can never appear" and the line Never appeared: "Moderate depression" — given when PHQ-9 total score < 10: every total below 10 is already caught by the "Mild depression" condition above it, so that band can never be reached. The table of combinations has no row with "Moderate depression".

Treat the list as a pointer to review, not a verdict:

  • It only looks at questions outside repeating groups.
  • It follows Show When rules: an answer to a question that is switched off is left out, as a person could not give it. A rule that reads a question it cannot try (a date, or a number without limits) is not judged.
  • It reads the results a calculation is written to give from its iif(...) branches, so a result produced another way is not checked.
  • On a very large form not every combination is tried, and the list says so.

Quality audit (advisory, separate from validation)

Alongside validation there's a separate Quality audit — a set of advisory checks that flag things which aren't strictly invalid FHIR but are usually authoring mistakes, e.g. an enableWhen condition that can never be true, or a choice item that would benefit from an answerValueSet binding it doesn't have. Unlike validation, the audit never blocks import or export — it's purely informational and only runs when you explicitly ask for it (⚙ Settings ▾ → Validate, with the Quality audit checkbox ticked in that menu). Its findings show up alongside the validation results but are visually distinct so they're never mistaken for errors that must be fixed before exporting.
